"},{"path":"/gas-price","method":"GET","description":"GAS_PRICE. Answers "what is gas right now on Ethereum", "how much does a transfer cost on Polygon", "are fees high on Base". "},{"path":"/wallet-balance","method":"GET","description":"WALLET_BALANCE_CHECK. Answers "how much ETH does 0xabc... hold", "what is the USDC balance of this address on Arbitrum". Params: address (required, 0x-prefixed, 40 hex characters), chain (optional, one of eth, base, arbitrum, polygon, default eth), token (optional, 0x-prefixed, 40 hex characters, an ERC-20 contract address; when supplied, returns that token's balance instead of the chain's native coin).
"},{"path":"/token-holders","method":"GET","description":"TOKEN_HOLDER_COUNT. Answers "how many wallets hold this token", "how many distinct addresses own 0xabc...". Takes a specific token contract address and returns the count of distinct holding addresses. This is a holder count, not price, supply or market data. Params: token (required, 0x-prefixed, 40 hex characters), chain (optional, one of eth, base, arbitrum, optimism, polygon, default eth).
"},{"path":"/tvl","method":"GET","description":"TVL_LOOKUP. Answers "what is the TVL of Aave", "how much value is locked in Uniswap", "what is total value locked on Ethereum". Takes a named DeFi protocol, pool or chain and returns the total value locked in it in USD. This is value locked, not market capitalisation. When both a protocol and a chain are supplied it returns that protocol's TVL on that chain alongside its total across all chains. Params: exactly one of protocol (a DefiLlama protocol slug, e.g. "uniswap") or tvl_chain (a free-text DefiLlama chain name, e.g. "Ethereum", covering DefiLlama's ~460 chains rather than only the five EVM chains above, which is why the param name differs from `chain`).
"},{"path":"/crypto-price","method":"GET","description":"CRYPTO_PRICE. Answers "what is Bitcoin worth", "price of ETH in USD", "how much is the token at 0xabc... trading for". Names a cryptocurrency asset and returns its current USD price, with 24-hour change and market cap where the feed supplies them, cross-checked across independent sources and reported with a source count. For the cost of transacting on a chain use GAS_PRICE instead. Params: either coin_id alone, or price_chain together with token. Exactly one of those two modes. Any coin named in words goes in coin_id, including a coin that shares its name with a chain: ether or Ethereum is coin_id="ethereum", and likewise "bitcoin", "solana". price_chain is only for pricing one specific contract, is never sent on its own, and always needs token (0x-prefixed, 40 hex characters, the token's contract address) alongside it, as in price_chain="base" with the contract to price. It also answers what a coin was worth on a past day: send that day as date ("2023-01-01"), in either mode, and the answer is the price on that date rather than the price now. Leave date off for the current price.
"},{"path":"/stock-price","method":"GET","description":"STOCK_PRICE. Answers "what is Apple trading at", "current share price of TSLA", "how much is NVDA stock". Names a listed equity or ticker and returns its current USD share price. It also answers what a stock was worth on a past day, such as "what did NVDA close at on 15 January 2024": send that day as date and the answer is the closing price on it, naming the last trading day before it when the market was shut that day. Params: ticker (required, a stock symbol, e.g. "AAPL") and date (optional, a past day as "2024-01-15"; leave it off for the current price).
"},{"path":"/ssl-check","method":"GET","description":"SSL_VERIFICATION. Answers "is the SSL certificate for example.com valid", "when does this domain's TLS certificate expire", "who issued the certificate for this host". Takes a hostname and reports the certificate that host is actually serving right now, from a real live TLS handshake performed at request time rather than a cached or certificate-transparency lookup, which disagree whenever a host still serves an old certificate. Reports a named verdict (valid, expired, self_signed, hostname_mismatch, untrusted), issuer, validity window, days to expiry, how many certificates the server presented and whether the chain reaches a trusted root, which name on the certificate the request matched, and the TLS version and cipher actually negotiated, flagging deprecated TLS 1.0/1.1 that will fail for modern clients whatever the certificate says. Params: domain (required, a bare hostname such as "example.com", a full URL, a host:port pair, or a question naming the domain).
"},{"path":"/weather-forecast","method":"GET","description":"WEATHER_FORECAST. Answers "what's the weather in Tokyo the next three days", "will it rain in London tomorrow", "how windy will it be in Cape Town on Friday", "will it snow in Oslo next week", and coordinate forms such as "what is the forecast at latitude 14.6042, longitude 120.9822 in 44 hours?". Accepts coordinates written out in full ("latitude 14.6042, longitude 120.9822"), a compact "lat,lon" pair, a place name, or the whole question, and answers the specific thing asked: the day or window named (right now, today, tonight, tomorrow, a weekday, this weekend, this week, in N hours, the next N days or hours) and the aspect emphasised (rain, wind, snow, storm, freeze, temperature), leading with a direct yes or no on that aspect the way a person would answer, then giving the expected condition in plain words, temperature range, precipitation total and chance of precipitation, snowfall, and peak wind speed with gusts and direction. Read live from the forecast service at request time. Params: location (required, coordinates in either form, a place name, or a whole question), days (optional, 1-16), when (optional, overrides the window parsed from the question), focus (optional, one of rain, wind, snow, storm, freeze, temperature).
"},{"path":"/storm-alert","method":"GET","description":"STORM_ALERT. Reports storm risk at a location over a stated window, answering questions of the form "what is the storm risk at latitude 14.6042, longitude 120.9822 in 44 hours?" and "what is the storm risk at latitude -5.1486, longitude 119.4319 right now?", as well as "is there a storm risk in Miami this weekend". Reports exactly what such a question asks for: wind speed, gusts, precipitation, and an overall risk between 0 and 1. Accepts coordinates written out in full ("latitude 14.6042, longitude 120.9822"), a compact "lat,lon" pair, a place name, or the whole question, and reads the window from it ("right now", "in N hours", "over the next 48 hours", "this weekend"). Alongside the 0-1 risk score a contract can threshold on, it returns a disruption grade (LOW/MODERATE/HIGH/SEVERE) from peak wind gust and its Beaufort force named in plain words, sustained wind speed and direction, total precipitation, forecast thunderstorm and hail hours, and the operational response that grade calls for. The window runs from the current hour forward, not from midnight, so the peak gust reported is always still ahead. Read live at request time. Params: location (required, coordinates in either form, a place name, or a whole question), hours (optional, default 48, also read from the question).
"},{"path":"/ip-geolocate","method":"GET","description":"IP_GEOLOCATION. Answers "where is 8.8.8.8 located", "what country is this IP address from", "is this IP a VPN or a datacenter". Takes an IPv4 or IPv6 address and reports its country, region, city, postal code, coordinates, timezone, and network owner with ASN, plus privacy and risk flags saying whether the address is a known proxy or VPN exit, a hosting or datacenter network, or a mobile carrier network, which is what fraud, bot-screening and geo-gating callers actually need. Read live at request time. Confidence is reported as 0.95 rather than 1.0 because IP geolocation is reliable to the country and only approximate to the city. Params: ip (required, a bare IPv4 or IPv6 address such as "8.8.8.8" or "2001:4860:4860::8888", or a whole question naming one).
"},{"path":"/academic-search","method":"GET","description":"ACADEMIC_SEARCH. Answers "find papers on federated learning", "peer-reviewed research on fraud detection since 2020". Takes a topic, or the whole question, and lists peer-reviewed journal articles on it in relevance order, with preprints, theses and datasets excluded, naming every paper found in the answer itself with its title, authors, publishing journal, year, citation count and DOI, plus a real excerpt from the leading paper's abstract and a note on which of the results is the most cited. A date range stated in the question ("since 2020", "between 2010 and 2020") is applied. Read live from OpenAlex, with Crossref as a fallback, at request time. Params: topic (required), limit (optional, 1-25, default 5), from_year (optional), to_year (optional).
"},{"path":"/web-search","method":"GET","description":"WEB_SEARCH. Answers an open question of any kind from a live web search performed at request time, for questions that have no single authoritative feed behind them: "what happened at the summit this week", "how does a heat pump work", "will El Nino disrupt shipping this season", "what did the company announce". Takes the whole question as the caller wrote it and returns a direct written answer followed by the sources it drew on, naming the most relevant three with their URLs. Questions about current events are searched against a news index and questions about markets and company results against a finance index, chosen from the wording of the question itself. Confidence is reported as 0.9 rather than 1.0 because a synthesized web answer is only as reliable as the pages behind it, unlike a chain read or a live TLS handshake. For a peer-reviewed literature search use ACADEMIC_SEARCH instead, and for a live number such as a price, gas fee, balance or forecast use the specific intent for it, which reads the value from its own provider rather than from the open web. Params: query (required, the whole question), max_results (optional, 1-20, default 5), topic_mode (optional, one of general, news, finance, overriding what the question implies).
"},{"path":"/content-extract","method":"GET","description":"CONTENT_EXTRACTION. Answers "what does this page say", "extract the text from this URL", "summarize the content at this link". Fetches a live URL at request time and returns its title and readable text, stripped of scripts, navigation, and markup. Params: url (required, a full http or https URL, a bare host such as github.com/torvalds, or a whole question containing one; also accepted as link or question). If the value is a passage of text with no URL, the dates, quantities, named entities and events are extracted from the text itself.
"},{"path":"/text-classify","method":"GET","description":"TEXT_CLASSIFICATION. Answers "what category is this text", "is this email spam or not", "classify this review as positive or negative". Takes a piece of text and returns the single best category it belongs to, with a brief reason. Params: text (required; also accepted as content or input), labels (optional, also accepted as categories or classes; comma-separated candidate categories the answer must pick from; if omitted, the category is chosen freely).
"},{"path":"/text-generate","method":"GET","description":"TEXT_GENERATION. Answers "write a short bio for a software engineer", "draft a product description for a water bottle". Takes an instruction or prompt and writes the requested text directly, with no preamble. Params: prompt (required).
"},{"path":"/language-generate","method":"GET","description":"LANGUAGE_GENERATION. Answers "translate this into French", "rewrite this in a formal tone", "paraphrase this sentence". Takes existing text and transforms it into another language, tone, or style. Params: text (required), target (optional, the target language/tone/style; also read from the instruction inside text when omitted).
"},{"path":"/research-synthesis","method":"GET","description":"RESEARCH_SYNTHESIS. Answers broader research questions such as "what are the main approaches to carbon capture" or "summarize the current state of quantum error correction". Combines multiple live web sources into one written synthesis, wider and more source-dense than WEB_SEARCH. Params: query (required; also q, question, topic, text), max_sources (optional, 1-20, default 10; also max_results, limit).
"},{"path":"/cross-chain-state","method":"GET","description":"CROSS_CHAIN_STATE_VERIFY. Answers "which chains is this address active on", "does this wallet exist on Base and Arbitrum", "is this a contract on any chain". Params: address (required, 0x-prefixed, 40 hex characters), chains (optional, comma-separated list restricting which chains are checked; defaults to every RPC-enabled chain). "},{"path":"/event-outcome","method":"GET","description":"EVENT_OUTCOME_RESOLUTION. Answers "did the merger go through", "who won the election", "was the proposal approved". Params: query (required; also q, question, event, market). "},{"path":"/weather-check","method":"GET","description":"WEATHER_CHECK. Answers "what's the weather like in Tokyo right now", "current temperature in London", "is it raining in Cape Town at the moment". "},{"path":"/language-translate","method":"GET","description":"LANGUAGE_TRANSLATION. Answers "translate 'good morning' into Japanese", "how do you say thank you in French". "},{"path":"/chat-complete","method":"GET","description":"CHAT_COMPLETION. Answers a message directly and conversationally, the way a chat assistant would, with no preamble. "},{"path":"/news-search","method":"GET","description":"NEWS_SEARCH. "},{"path":"/news-headlines","method":"GET","description":"NEWS_HEADLINES. Answers "what are today's headlines on the election", "top news about the central bank". Returns a short list of current headlines on a named topic, each with its source URL. "},{"path":"/fact-check","method":"GET","description":"FACT_CHECK. Answers "is it true that X", "fact check this claim: ...". Params: claim (required; also statement, text, query, q, question). "},{"path":"/sentiment-analyze","method":"GET","description":"SENTIMENT_ANALYSIS. Answers "is this review positive or negative", "what's the sentiment of this message". Classifies text as exactly one of Positive, Negative, Neutral or Mixed, with a short reason. Also answers "what is the general sentiment toward X" for a named company, token or event. Params: text (required; also accepted as content, review, message or comment).
"},{"path":"/content-moderate","method":"GET","description":"CONTENT_MODERATION. Answers "does this text violate policy", "is this message safe to post". Params: text (required; also accepted as content, message, comment or post).
"},{"path":"/cve-lookup","method":"GET","description":"CVE_LOOKUP. Answers "what is CVE-2021-44228", "known vulnerabilities in log4j". "},{"path":"/telegraph-knowledge","method":"GET","description":"TELEGRAPH_KNOWLEDGE. Params: question (required, also accepted as query, q, text, input).
"},{"path":"/text-summarize","method":"GET","description":"TEXT_SUMMARIZATION. Summarizes supplied text to a given length or style, or a sensible default when none is named. Params: text (required), length (optional, e.g. "50 words" or "one sentence").
"},{"path":"/chatbot-conversation","method":"GET","description":"CHATBOT_CONVERSATION. Replies to a chat message, using a supplied messages/history array as context when given. Params: message (required), messages (optional, a JSON array of {role, content} turns, also accepted as history).
"},{"path":"/semantic-similarity","method":"GET","description":"SEMANTIC_SIMILARITY. Returns a 0-1 semantic similarity score and a short reason for two supplied texts. Params: text1, text2 (required, also accepted as a and b).
"},{"path":"/grammar-spell-check","method":"GET","description":"GRAMMAR_SPELL_CHECK. Returns corrected text plus a count and list of the grammar and spelling fixes made. Params: text (required).
"},{"path":"/ai-text-detect","method":"GET","description":"AI_TEXT_DETECTION. Returns an approximate self-assessment of how likely supplied text is AI-generated, with named cues and an honest disclaimer that this is a language-model estimate, not a certified detector. Params: text (required).
"},{"path":"/research-query","method":"GET","description":"RESEARCH_QUERY. Answers an open research question from live web sources in one well-sourced paragraph. Params: query (required, also accepted as q, question, topic, text, research, search, prompt, subject), max_results (optional, 1-20, default 6).
"},{"path":"/threat-intelligence","method":"GET","description":"THREAT_INTELLIGENCE. "},{"path":"/package-status","method":"GET","description":"PACKAGE_STATUS. "},{"path":"/url-scan","method":"GET","description":"URL_SCAN. Params: url (required, also accepted as link, website, target, query, q, question, text, input).
"},{"path":"/currency-exchange","method":"GET","description":"CURRENCY_EXCHANGE. Answers "how much is 100 dollars in euros", "convert 50 GBP to JPY", using live ECB reference rates. Params: from, to (currency codes or names such as "dollars", "euros"), amount (optional, default 1).
"},{"path":"/fx-now","method":"GET","description":"FX_NOW. Params: from (also base), to (also symbols, quote_currency), both currency codes or names such as "dollars", "euros"; amount (optional, default 1); or the whole question as query.
"},{"path":"/sanctions-screening","method":"GET","description":"SANCTIONS_SCREENING_MATCH. Answers "is John Doe sanctioned", "check this company against the OFAC list". "},{"path":"/vulnerability-triage","method":"GET","description":"VULNERABILITY_TRIAGE. Answers "how urgent is CVE-2021-44228", "should I patch log4j now". "},{"path":"/sports-score","method":"GET","description":"SPORTS_SCORE. Answers "what is the score of the Lakers game". "},{"path":"/game-result","method":"GET","description":"GAME_RESULT. Answers "who won the Knicks game". Winner of a named team's most recently completed match, via TheSportsDB, with a live web-search fallback for teams outside its coverage. Params: team (required, a club or franchise name).
"},{"path":"/route-eta","method":"GET","description":"ROUTE_ETA. Answers "how long to drive from London to Paris", "what is the distance between Miami and Orlando".
